_comment: Race Week configurable prize pools. Read FRESH at every Monday roll and by cd-raceweekprizes reroll - edit any time, no restart needed. An empty/missing pool falls back to the automatic rule (CR band for car rungs, pack tier for pack rungs, base/rare rotation for 250, random secret driver for the exclusive rung). Invalid IDs are skipped with a console warning. Serialised drivers are never valid ladder prizes.

_rules.carPool: list of carIDs - ANY car is allowed (BM/reference cards, bosses, anything that exists)
_rules.driverPool: list of driverIDs (serialised drivers are never valid ladder prizes)
_rules.pool_entries: Every pool (carPool/packPool/driverPool, in rungs AND in endless) takes either a bare ID ("c03652") or a weighted entry ({ "id": "c03652", "weight": 9 }). Weight defaults to 1, so a plain list is a uniform roll. Weights are RELATIVE shares and never need to sum to anything — 7/3, 0.7/0.3 and 700/300 are all the same 70/30 split. Decimals are fine (0.5 is half a share, 0.05 is about 5%). A weight of exactly 0 DISABLES that entry (park it without deleting the line); if every entry is 0 the pool counts as empty and the automatic rule takes over. Missing weight = 1. Mixing forms is fine. Listing an ID twice also doubles its chance, which is the easy way to do small ratios. NOTE: an "ordered" pool IGNORES weights — it is a fixed weekly rotation, so repeat an entry to give it more weeks.
_rules.ordered: true on any rung = its pools cycle by ISO week number IN LIST ORDER instead of random; the same week index is used across all pools in that rung, so equal-length carPool+driverPool lists pair up for themed weeks (the exclusive rung ships ordered)
_rules.money: money amount for the rung (25-rung override, or part of a custom rung)
_rules.endless_rungs: Past the top fixed rung, a rung lands every 50 wins automatically and rolls its own prize kind (pack/car/driver by weight, see ENDLESS in consts/raceWeek.js). Adding that win count here OVERRIDES the random roll for that rung, exactly like any other. Tuning the interval, ceiling or weights is a code change, not a config one.
_rules.custom_rungs: add ANY numeric key (e.g. "20") with at least one pool/money to create a new threshold rung - applies at the next Monday roll, or immediately via cd-raceweekprizes reroll all. Custom rungs are normal races (never boss gates). Remove the key + reroll all to retire it. Players already past the rung's win count that week won't retro-claim it.
_rules.rung_250: driverPool list order IS the weekly rotation order (always ordered)
_rules.events: curated packPool per pack-granting in-race event (packshards / goldenopponent), read fresh at EVERY event resolution - no reroll needed, edits apply to the next drop. Empty pool = automatic roll across every standard-tier pack (event/limited packs included, so curate these once you care)
_rules.weeks: PRE-PROGRAMMED WEEKS. Two key forms: "2026-W44" fires that exact week once, "44" fires week 44 of EVERY year. Exact beats recurring. Inside a week, any rung key overrides that rung's pools for that week only - every rung you DON'T list falls back to "rungs" below exactly as normal, so you only script what you care about. Meta keys: _label (shown in the announcement title), _description (replaces the default blurb), _color (hex, themes the embed). Any key starting with _ is ignored by the prize resolver. Scheduled weeks are resolved at the Monday roll, so edits land at the next rollover or immediately via cd-raceweekprizes reroll all.

_PARKED-fast-and-furious._status: PARKED — inactive. This key starts with _ so the resolver ignores it entirely. To arm it, rename the key back to a week key like "2026-W35" (that exact week) or "35" (week 35 every year), then it fires at the next Monday roll.
_PARKED-fast-and-furious._comment: FAST & FURIOUS WEEK — originally Mon 24 Aug to Sun 30 Aug 2026, postponed, marking 25 years of the first film. Meta only for now: NO rung keys are set, so every rung runs on its normal pool from "rungs" below. Add rung keys ONLY when you have the prize picked — see _howToAddPrizes.
_PARKED-fast-and-furious._howToAddPrizes: A rung key here REPLACES that rung's normal config for the week, wholesale. So "400": { "carPool": [] } does NOT mean 'leave it alone' — an empty pool falls back to the AUTOMATIC rule and you lose the curated prize. Either give the rung a real pool, or leave the key out entirely. Shape to copy: "400": { "carPool": ["cXXXXX"], "driverPool": ["dXXXXX"] } · "50": { "carPool": ["cXXXXX"] } · "200": { "packPool": ["pXXXXX"] } · "25": { "money": 500000 }
_PARKED-fast-and-furious._description: Twenty-five years since a green Eclipse and an orange Supra taught everyone what a quarter mile is. It's not about the prizes. It's about family.

_example._comment: Keys starting with _ are ignored. Copy this shape, rename to "2026-W44" (one-off) or "44" (every year), and it goes live at the next roll.
_example._description: The lights are off at the circuit and something out there is running quicker lap times than it has any right to.

endless._comment: THE ENDLESS TAIL. Past the last fixed rung a prize lands every `step` wins, up to `max`. Each of those rungs rolls its KIND from `weights` at the Monday roll, then draws from the matching pool below. Read fresh like everything else here — no restart.
endless._pools: Weighted entries work here too ({ "id": "cXXXXX", "weight": 5 }) — see pool_entries in _rules. Empty pool = automatic roll (strong Normal cars 850+, elite packs, any in-rotation base/rare driver). Fill one to curate exactly what can drop, same as the rung pools below. Drivers flagged inRotation:false are NEVER dropped automatically — that protects Ragnar Voss, The Rookie and the secret-rung driver — but listing one in driverPool here WILL hand it out, so be deliberate.
endless._override: To pin a single endless rung, just add its win count to "rungs" below (e.g. "750": { "carPool": ["cXXXXX"] }). A configured rung always beats the random roll.
endless._weights: Relative, not percentages — they are normalised. { pack: 60, car: 30, driver: 10 } gives 60/30/10; { pack: 1, car: 1, driver: 0 } gives a 50/50 car-or-pack split and no drivers.
